name: Toronto
tagline: Canada's largest and most multicultural city, a genuine United Nations of neighbourhoods anchored by a tower that dominated the world's skylines for over three decades.
highlight: Standing on the CN Tower's glass floor, 342 metres of open air the only thing between your feet and the street below.
shortDescription: Canada's largest and most multicultural city, home to the CN Tower, the Distillery District's Victorian warehouses and neighbourhoods representing the world.
metaDescription: A Toronto travel guide: the CN Tower, the Distillery District, Kensington Market, Casa Loma, food and how to plan a visit to Canada's biggest city.
knownFor: The CN Tower, Kensington Market, the Distillery District

image.file: File:CN Tower, Toronto, Canada (Unsplash DJ kOgH5u0o).jpg
image.alt: The CN Tower above Toronto's skyline

intro: Toronto is Canada's largest city and its most multicultural, with over half its population born outside Canada and neighbourhoods representing nearly every corner of the world.
Its skyline is still defined by the CN Tower, which held the record for the world's tallest freestanding structure for more than three decades.
The real draw, though, is street level — Kensington Market's eclectic shops, the Distillery District's Victorian warehouses, and a food scene that reflects the city's remarkable diversity.

whyVisit.intro: Toronto's case rests on being one of the world's most diverse cities, with the food and neighbourhood culture to prove it.

points.title: It's one of the most multicultural cities on Earth
points.text: Neighbourhoods representing dozens of cultures, each with its own genuine character.

points.title: The CN Tower is still an icon
points.text: A defining symbol of the skyline, with a glass floor and revolving restaurant.

points.title: The food scene is exceptional
points.text: A direct reflection of the city's diversity, from dim sum to Jamaican patties to fine dining.

points.title: It's a real, walkable big city
points.text: Distinct neighbourhoods connect easily by transit or on foot.

points.title: It works well as an Eastern Canada base
points.text: An easy pairing with Niagara Falls, Montreal and Quebec City.

attractionsIntro: Toronto's essential sights are spread across its downtown core and a handful of distinct historic neighbourhoods.

attractions.name: The CN Tower

image.file: File:CN Tower, Toronto, Canada (Unsplash DJ kOgH5u0o).jpg

attractions.text: The city's defining landmark, held the record for the world's tallest freestanding structure from 1975 to 2007.
attractions.tip: Book a sunset time slot for the best light over Lake Ontario.

attractions.name: The Distillery District
attractions.text: A car-free enclave of Victorian industrial architecture, once the largest whisky distillery in the British Empire.
attractions.tip: A lovely spot for a slow wander among galleries, boutiques and cafés.

attractions.name: Casa Loma

image.alt: Casa Loma, a castle in Toronto

attractions.text: A full-scale early 20th-century castle, complete with secret passages and manicured gardens.
attractions.tip: Allow a couple of hours to properly explore both the interior and the grounds.

attractions.name: St Lawrence Market

image.file: File:St Lawrence Market, Toronto, West partial view 20170417 1.jpg

attractions.text: A working market with real history, once named the world's best food market by National Geographic.
attractions.tip: Visit on a Saturday for the additional farmers' market in the north building.

attractions.name: Kensington Market
attractions.text: One of the city's most eclectic neighbourhoods, vintage shops and global food stalls packed into a few colourful blocks.
attractions.tip: Visit on a car-free Pedestrian Sunday if your dates align, held on the last Sunday of warmer months.

attractions.name: The Toronto Islands

image.file: File:View of Toronto Skyline from Centre Island.jpg
image.alt: Toronto's skyline seen from the Toronto Islands

attractions.text: A car-free escape a short ferry ride from downtown, with beaches, parkland and the city's best skyline view.
attractions.tip: Rent a bike on the islands to cover more ground than walking alone.

attractions.name: The Royal Ontario Museum's Crystal

image.alt: The Michael Lee-Chin Crystal at the Royal Ontario Museum

attractions.text: A striking architectural statement, a jagged crystalline extension bursting from the museum's original heritage building.
attractions.tip: Allow a full afternoon — the collection inside is extensive.

thingsToDoIntro: Toronto rewards exploring by neighbourhood, each with its own distinct food and character.

thingsToDo.title: Go up the CN Tower

image.file: File:Toronto - ON - CN Tower bei Nacht2.jpg

thingsToDo.text: An essential Toronto experience, taking in the view from the observation deck or glass floor.
thingsToDo.tip: Consider the EdgeWalk if you want a real adrenaline rush — a hands-free walk around the tower's outer rim.

thingsToDo.title: Wander the Distillery District's cobblestones

image.alt: Cobblestone streets in the Distillery District

thingsToDo.text: A relaxed way to spend an afternoon, browsing boutiques and galleries in converted Victorian warehouses.
thingsToDo.tip: Check the events calendar — the district regularly hosts markets and festivals.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Casa Loma's castle rooms
thingsToDo.text: A fun, slightly surreal visit, wandering a full-scale castle's period rooms and secret tunnel.
thingsToDo.tip: Check for seasonal light shows and special events held on the grounds.

thingsToDo.title: Browse St Lawrence Market's food stalls

image.alt: Food stalls at St Lawrence Market

thingsToDo.text: An essential food stop, sampling everything from peameal bacon sandwiches to international specialties.
thingsToDo.tip: Go hungry and share several stalls' offerings rather than filling up at just one.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Kensington Market's eclectic shops
thingsToDo.text: A colourful way to spend a few hours, vintage stores and global street food packed into a compact area.
thingsToDo.tip: Pair with neighbouring Chinatown, just a short walk away.

thingsToDo.title: Take the ferry to the Toronto Islands

image.file: File:Toronto Islands Yacht Club and Skyline.jpg
image.alt: The ferry to the Toronto Islands

thingsToDo.text: An easy, scenic escape, swapping downtown streets for beaches and the city's best skyline photo.
thingsToDo.tip: Book ferry tickets online ahead on busy summer weekends.

foodIntro: Toronto's food reflects its remarkable diversity, a real strength of the city's dining scene.

foods.name: Peameal bacon sandwich

image.alt: A peameal bacon sandwich, a Toronto specialty

foods.text: A true Toronto original, cornmeal-crusted back bacon piled onto a soft bun.
foods.whereToTry: St Lawrence Market's Carousel Bakery, the dish's most famous source.

foods.name: Jamaican beef patty
foods.text: A beloved staple reflecting Toronto's large Caribbean community.
foods.whereToTry: Bakeries and shops throughout the city, especially in Caribbean neighbourhoods.

foods.name: Butter tarts

image.file: File:Butter tarts it's a Canadian thing. (47104703864).jpg
image.alt: Butter tarts, a classic Canadian pastry

foods.text: A beloved Ontario classic, found at bakeries throughout the city.

foods.name: Poutine

image.alt: Poutine, Canada's fries, cheese curds and gravy dish

foods.text: Widely available, though this is Quebec's dish rather than a local specialty.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants and food trucks throughout the city.

foods.name: Dim sum

image.file: File:Three dim sum in steamer basket.jpg

foods.text: Excellent here too, a reflection of Toronto's own large Chinese community.

foods.name: Ontario craft beer and wine
foods.text: Worth exploring, with a thriving local brewery scene and Niagara wine country nearby.
foods.whereToTry: Bars and restaurants throughout the city.

accommodation.intro: Toronto offers accommodation for every budget, with downtown commanding the highest prices.

areas.name: Downtown or the Entertainment District
areas.bestFor: Being within walking distance of the CN Tower and waterfront
areas.text: The most convenient, though also the priciest, part of the city to stay.

areas.name: Queen West or Kensington
areas.bestFor: A more character-filled, slightly better value stay
areas.text: Close to Kensington Market and Chinatown, with easy transit downtown.

gettingThere.intro: Toronto is one of North America's best-connected cities by air, with a large international airport.

options.detail: The UP Express train connects Pearson Airport to downtown Union Station in about 25 minutes.
Via Rail's corridor service connects all three cities well.

options.mode: Bus or drive from Niagara Falls
options.detail: About 1.5 hours by road or a direct GO Transit train.

gettingAround.intro: Toronto's extensive transit network covers the city well, with downtown itself easily walkable.

options.text: Reliable and easy to use across the city.
options.detail: The TTC's subway lines and streetcar network cover most major sights.

options.text: The best way to explore individual downtown neighbourhoods.
options.detail: Kensington Market, the Distillery District and the waterfront are all walkable once you're there.

options.text: The only way to reach the islands.
options.detail: Frequent departures from the downtown ferry terminal.

bestTime.headline: May to September for warm weather and outdoor events
bestTime.summary: Toronto is a year-round city, with summer bringing the most festivals and outdoor activity.

seasons.text: Mild, comfortable weather before summer's full heat and humidity arrive.
Warm and humid, with the city's festival calendar in full swing.
Comfortable temperatures with excellent fall colour in the city's parks.
Cold, with the city's extensive PATH underground walkway system a real asset.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — Toronto works as a year-round city break.

itinerary.title: Three days in Toronto
itinerary.intro: Built around downtown's landmarks, historic neighbourhoods and a day trip to the islands.

days.title: Downtown and the CN Tower
days.afternoon: St Lawrence Market for lunch and browsing.
days.evening: Dinner and drinks in the Distillery District.

days.title: Neighbourhoods and Casa Loma
days.summary: A day of distinct city character.
days.afternoon: Tour Casa Loma's castle rooms and gardens.
days.evening: Dinner reflecting the city's global food scene.

days.title: The Toronto Islands
days.summary: A relaxed day on the water.
days.afternoon: Cycle or walk the islands, with the skyline view.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Toronto visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book CN Tower tickets online ahead, especially for sunset time slots.
Use the PATH underground walkway system in winter to avoid the cold.
Explore by neighbourhood — Toronto's real character lives outside downtown's tower district.
Book Toronto Islands ferry tickets ahead on busy summer weekends.
Try food from multiple different neighbourhoods rather than sticking to downtown alone.
Use Toronto as a base for day trips to Niagara Falls.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Toronto?
faq.a: Three days covers the city's main sights and a couple of its distinct neighbourhoods comfortably.
Comparable to other major North American cities, with food covering a wide range of budgets.
Yes — downtown and its surrounding neighbourhoods are compact and well served by transit.

faq.q: Is the CN Tower worth visiting?
faq.a: Yes — it remains an iconic experience, and the glass floor is a memorable thrill.

faq.q: Can you day-trip to Niagara Falls from Toronto?
faq.a: Yes, easily — it's about 1.5 hours by road or a direct train.
Yes, exceptional — its multicultural population makes it one of North America's best cities for diverse, authentic cuisine.
